Title: Region-hybrid batch + low-latency capacity sizer (worked example)
Summary:
This is a working capacity sizer for Private/VPC deployments that expect a mix of low-latency interactive traffic (P95 <= 120ms) and periodic high-throughput batch workloads (offline embeddings, bulk reranking). The sheet walks through a heuristic sizing approach, three scenarios (conservative / typical / aggressive), and a lightweight BOM estimate that balances density, redundancy, and cost. This is an iterative planning artifact — expect ~2–3 rounds with infra/product before final procurement.

Key assumptions (call these out early)
- Primary region: us-west-2 (customer can swap region/pricing). Secondary/failover region: eu-west-1
- Representative model: 70B decoder-only quantized variant (8-bit/4-bit profiles). Serve variant throughput estimates below.
- Low-latency workload: median request length 30 tokens, tail (P95) 120 tokens. Target P95 latency <=120ms for interactive tier.
- Batch workload: offline bulk jobs (embedding + rerank) with sustained token throughput windows (e.g., 5–10 minutes bursts).
- Expected SLO split: 70% interactive, 30% batch by request count (cost dominated by tokens).
- Target utilization bands (usable GPU): 50% steady for low-latency capacity, allow 80–95% utilization during batch-only windows via autoscaling/burst.
- Network egress and storage estimate is separate; this file focuses on GPU compute & infra (servers, NVMe, switching, rack power/cooling headroom).

Throughput/per-GPU heuristics (sample nu:
- H100 80GB (fp16/quantized path): ~1000 tokens/sec sustained for 70B with batching and KV cache reuse (batch-friendly). For low-latency single request paths, approximate effective throughput = 250 tokens/sec (because of smaller batches, context overhead).
- A100 80GB: ~600 tokens/sec batch, ~180 tokens/sec interactive
- A10G: ~220 tokens/sec batch, ~60 tokens/sec interactive
Note: these are coarse; run a microbenchmark container in customer environment to get real numbers.
Variables and shorthand used in formulas:
- R = peak concurrent interactive requests (requests/sec arriving during steady peak window)
- L_med = median tokens per interactive request
- L_p95 = P95 tokens per interactive request
- T_int = acceptable P95 latency (s)
- TP_gpu_int = interactive effective tokens/sec a GPU can serve (depends on model + batching)
- TP_gpu_batch = batch tokens/sec a GPU can do when fully saturated for long windows
- G_int = GPUs reserved for interactive capacity
- G_batch = GPUs for batch work (can be separate or preemptible on same fleet)
- margin = operational headroom (typical 1.2–1.5)
Sizing interactive capacity (heuristic):
1) Estimate peak interactive qps (R). Example: R = 120 req/s
2) Choose conservative tokens for P95 path (use L_p95). Example L_p95 = 120 tokens
3) Required sustained tokens/sec to meet latency target: S_required = R * L_p95
4) GPUs for interactive = ceil( (S_required / TP_gpu_int) * margin )
Example (us-west-2 baseline):
- R = 120 req/s, L_p95 = 120 tokens => S_required = 14,400 tokens/sec
- Choose HW: A100 (TP_gpu_int = 180 tokens/sec)
- margin = 1.3
- G_int = ceil( (14400 / 180) * 1.3 ) = ceil(80 * 1.3) = ceil(104) = 104 GPUs
Notes: 104 GPUs across availability zones; aim for N+1 redundancy per AZ and room for host failures.
Sizing batch capacity (heuristic):
Batch jobs are elastic and can be scheduled into quieter periods. Two options:
- Dedicated batch pool (separate servers/G_batch)
- Burst onto interactive fleet when utilization allows (requires preemption/fair-share)
Sizing approach (dedicated):
1) Decide target batch sustained tokens/sec during bulk window. Example: aim for 200k tokens/sec sustained.
2) Choose TP_gpu_batch (A100 ~600)
3) margin for scheduling overhead = 1.15
4) G_batch = ceil((200000 / 600) * 1.15) = ceil(333.33 * 1.15) = ceil(383.33) = 384 GPUs
Hybrid approach example (cost-optimized):
- Reserve G_int = 80 GPUs for interactive (sized for typical but not worst-case P95)
- Provision G_shared_spare = 40 GPUs as preemptible burst pool that can help interactive in tail events and run batch when idle
- Dedicated batch fleet = 160 GPUs for regular bulk jobs
Total GPUs = 280 (vs 104+384 = 488 if fully separate)
Rationale: this reduces BOM while retaining tail capacity through preemption and autoscale policies.
Region distribution and redundancy:
- Start with primary region containing 70% of capacity, secondary with 30% as warm failover.
- Example for hybrid total = 280 GPUs: primary 196 GPUs, secondary 84 GPUs
- Place across 3 AZs in the region, use AZ-aware placement: 40/40/40 (primary) + 20/20/20 (secondary split) depending on server granularity.
Server and rack planning (density):
- Target server config (density tradeoffs):
  - 4x H100 or A100 per 1U/2U chassis (varies by vendor). Typical high-density: 8 GPUs/2U with OAM-style servers. We pick a conservative 4x A100 per 1U equivalent for power/cooling sanity.
  - Server framing: 4x GPUs + 2x 3.8TB NVMe (OS + local cache) + 2x 1.6TB NVMe for checkpoints + 2x 100GbE NIC
- Rack population: 42U usable -> with 2U servers = 21 servers per rack. At 4 GPUs/server = 84 GPUs per rack.
Example mapping (using 4x-A100 server):
- To support 280 GPUs: ceil(280 / 84) = ceil(3.333) = 4 racks -> 336 GPU capacity (offers N+spare)
- Usable after failures/maintenance: plan for 20% headroom -> effective target ~268 available GPUs.
BOM estimate (worked numbers \u2014 repl:
- A100 80GB GPU card, OEM unit cost (list): $28,000
- GPU server chassis (4x GPU, dual-socket, 2x NIC, NVMe): $25,000 per server
- Top-of-rack 100GbE switch (redundant pair per rack): $18,000 per switch => $36,000 per rack
- Rack PDUs, power distribution, cabling: $6,000 per rack
- On-prem KMS appliance/ HSM: $35,000
- Remote management + BMC licensing (per rack): $3,000
- Rack + installation + contingency (per rack): $10,000
Sample cost calc (4 racks, 21 servers/rack):
- GPUs required for 4 racks at 84 GPUs/rack = 336 GPUs (we only need 280 but rack granularity drives purchase)
- GPU unit cost total = 336 * $28,000 = $9,408,000
- Servers = (336 GPUs / 4 per server) = 84 servers -> 84 * $25,000 = $2,100,000
- Switches = 4 racks * $36,000 = $144,000
- PDUs/cabling = 4 * $6,000 = $24,000
- KMS + mgmt + rack install contingency = $35,000 + (4 * $3,000) + (4 * $10,000) = $35,000 + $12,000 + $40,000 = $87,000
- Subtotal hardware = $11,843,000
- Logistics/procurement/taxes (~10%) = $1,184,300
- Total order estimate = ~$13,027,300
Operational OPEX considerations (rough):
- Power draw estimate: A100 80GB server (4x GPUs) ~ 4–5 kW per server under load (varies). For 84 servers -> ~350–420 kW (rack-level cooling needed)
- Maintenance contract (~10–15% of hardware/year) -> budget accordingly
- Cloud-burst fallback costs if traffic spikes beyond physical capacity (include runway in contract for hosted fallback)
Tradeoffs and notes (ops / SRE):
- Higher density reduces rack count and idle spare GPUs but increases risk when a host goes down (larger loss per failure).
- Using preemptible/shared pool reduces overprovisioning but requires fine-grained autoscale + request prioritization.
- If P95 latency matters more than cost, bias toward more interactive-headroom (larger G_int; smaller batch pool).
- For regulated customers, ensure KMS and audit logging hardware are included in procurement scope.
Three scenario summary (rounded):
- Conservative (SLO-first): 400 GPUs, 5 racks, target P95 headroom, cost ~ $15–18M
- Typical (balanced - recommended for most customers): 280 GPUs, 4 racks, hybrid shared/batch, cost ~ $12–13M
- Aggressive growth-ready: 560 GPUs, 7 racks, multi-region active-active, cost ~ $22–26M
